author: Coral Murphy Marcos
description:
President’s latest order expected to bring NIH funding under control of Trump administration to align with agenda

Donald Trump’s latest executive order is expected to establish a board responsible for approving National Institutes of Health grant funding, marking another attempt by the Trump administration to censor topics that do not align with the president’s agenda.

The executive order, reported by outlets including the Washington Post and Politico, was discussed in a meeting on Friday where senior administration officials accused the NIH of funding “woke” initiatives that went against Trump’s political priorities
title: Trump reportedly to form health funding board that could veto ‘woke’ initiatives

author: Australian Associated Press
description:
Australia and Finland are vying for a spot on the council, and the PM needs two thirds of member states to back him

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Anthony Albanese launched a formal bid for Australia to serve a two-year term on the UN security council in 2029 and 2030.

Albanese also unveiled former News Corp head of broadcasting Siobhan McKenna as Australia’s next consul general to New York.
title: Albanese launches bid for UN security council seat and names former Murdoch aide to top diplomatic post

author: Guardian staff
description:
Follow the day’s news live.

The trial of a former NSW police officer accused of murdering two men is set to begin in Sydney.

Beau Lamarre-Condon has pleaded not guilty to two counts of murder and one charge of aggravated break and enter over the deaths of TV presenter Jesse Baird, 26, and his partner Luke Davies, 29, in February 2024.

His case has faced ongoing delays since charges were laid, but today, the 31-year-old’s trial will finally get underway.

On Monday, a jury will be selected at NSW supreme court on King Street.

Depending on how long the empanelment process takes the court may hear the crown’s opening statement in the afternoon.

Justice Natalie Adams will preside over the trial, which is slated to go for two to three months and include a brief of evidence with more than 200 witnesses.

The case has received significant media attention and Lamarre-Condon’s trial is also expected to attract substantial public inte
title: Australia news live: Albanese names former News Corp executive as consul-general in New York

author: Charlie Moloney
description:
Jane Adetoro, Christina Walters and Rebecca Walters from Uxbridge were found on 13 May

The deaths of three sisters found in the sea off Brighton beach did not involve any criminality or third-party involvement, police have concluded.

The bodies of Jane Adetoro, 36, Christina Walters, 32, and Rebecca Walters, 31, from Uxbridge, west London, were found on 13 May. A postmortem conducted that month confirmed all three women died by drowning.

Continue reading...
title: Deaths of three women in sea at Brighton had no criminal involvement, police say

author: Ed Pilkington
description:
Florida’s María Elvira Salazar warns Trump that advisers are ‘compromising his legacy’ and not showing ‘whole picture’

María Elvira Salazar, the Republican congresswoman who has accused the president of going too far on immigration enforcement, doubled down on her criticism of the administration on Sunday, warning Donald Trump that some of his advisers were “compromising his legacy”.

In an interview with CBS News’s Face the Nation, the Florida representative who is locked in a tight race for re-election pleaded with the US president not to “squander” his
title: House Republican doubles down on jab at Trump’s immigration enforcement

author: Peter Walker and Alexandra Topping
description:
Ed Davey’s party made a series of proposals as concern grows among members that voters don’t know what its policies are or what it stands for

The Liberal Democrats have used their conference to unveil a £2bn plan to cut fuel duty, part of a series of policy proposals intended to tackle worries that not enough voters know what Ed Davey’s party stands for.

The proposal to cut fuel duty by 10p a litre for a fixed three-month period came as polling showed Lib Dem policies are less well known than those of Restore Britain, which only launched as a political party in February and has one MP – Rupert Lowe – to their 71.
title: Lib Dems use conference to set out £2bn plan to cut fuel duty

author: Hannah Al-Othman
description:
Wife of former PM takes part in designer Edeline Lee’s show inspired by the Greek myth of Sisyphus

Victoria Starmer has taken part in a London fashion week show, in one of her first public appearances since her husband, Keir Starmer, stepped down as prime minister.

Lady Starmer appeared at Sunday’s Edeline Lee show. The London-based, Canadian British designer’s clothes are a favourite of the Princess of Wales, and have also been worn by celebrities including singer Taylor Swift and actor and screenwriter Phoebe Waller-Bridge.

Continue reading...
title: Victoria Starmer models clothes at London fashion week show

author: Sarah Martin Senior correspondent
description:
Exclusive: James Ashby also drives new Ford Ranger given to party and is main pilot of plane donated by Gina Rinehart, which he says are not for personal use

  • Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast

Pauline Hanson’s right-hand man, James Ashby, is enjoying generous benefits as a result of his role working for One Nation, with documents showing that a company linked to the party built a $56,000 shed on his central Queensland property.

Guardian Australia understands that Ashby, formerly Hanson’s chief of staff and now the party’s national director, also drives a new Ford Ranger that was “personally” gifted to One Nation by Hancock Agriculture’s chief executive, Adam Giles, in April. Hanson said the vehicle woul
title: One Nation-linked company built $56,000 shed on private property of Pauline Hanson’s right-hand man

author: Ben Quinn Political correspondent
description:
Action against Ofcom comes as social media companies are being accused of using courts to slow down implementation

Meta has launched a fresh legal challenge against Britain’s media regulator in the latest of a slew of actions by social media companies who are accused of using the courts to slow down implementation of the Online Safety Act.

Lawyers for the parent company of Facebook served notice during the week in an appeal against placing WhatsApp and Instagram, which are also owned by Meta, in a category that subjects them to additional duties.

Continue reading...
title: Meta launches legal challenge against UK media regulator over Online Safety Act

author: Alex Lawson
description:
Unit1 hopes to offer cheaper version of shows such as Abba Voyage, showcasing living and dead artists in any venue

The former chief executive of Andrew Lloyd Webber’s entertainment group has obtained a near-£15m investment for his UK music tech startup that hopes to recreate classic concerts by manifesting musicians as digital avatars.

Unit1 was set up last year by Barney Wragg, an entertainment executive who ran Lord Lloyd-Webber’s Cats-to-Evita empire for five years from late 2011. It has secured the $20m in funding from a group of investors, including tech backer Balderton Capital through its partner Daniel Waterhouse, who made early investments in Spotify.

Continue reading...
title: UK startup snares $20m to recreate gigs with ‘hyper-realistic’ digital avatars

author: Haroon Siddique Legal affairs correspondent
description:
Data raid comes amid targeting of lifeboat charity by far-right agitators who object to migrant boat rescues

Supporters of the Royal National Lifeboat Institution (RNLI) have been warned that their personal information could have been stolen by hackers amid targeting of the charity by far-right agitators.

In a letter accompanying the autumn copy of its Lifeboat magazine, the charity warned members that their “name, contact details and records of interactions with the RNLI” could have been breached in the raid on a company it uses for customer relationship management.

Continue reading...
title: RNLI warns supporters their personal information may have been hacked

author: Lisa O’Carroll Senior correspondent
description:
Rafael Moreno, whose company has opened demo plant in Brazil, says market is ‘nervous’ as Trump-Xi summit looms

The head of a mining company hoping to supply the EU with rare earths in two years’ time has said it is “paramount” to end China’s stranglehold on the supply of the raw materials used in everything from cars to wind turbines and military jets.

As Donald Trump and China’s president, Xi Jinping, prepare to meet on Thursday in their second summit of the year, Rafael Moreno said it was also “imperative” that they do a deal for Beijing to ease up, once again, on its threat to ban exports of rare earths.

Continue reading...
title: China’s stranglehold on rare earths must be ended, says hopeful supplier to EU

author: Joseph Gedeon in Washington
description:
It’s not clear that financial interests are driving White House policy, but they run parallel even as resistance mounts

Donald Trump’s sons, through a series of AI-linked defense and technology ventures, have picked up a $620m Pentagon loan, a Marine Corps robotics contract and an undisclosed air force drone deal in the past year. His longtime friend Michael Dell won a Pentagon contract worth nearly $9bn. And this week, as public support for artificial intelligence sinks to some of the lowest levels ever recorded, the president went to bat for the industry. .

“The only control or ‘guardrails’ that AI needs is a STRONG AND SMART (High IQ!) PRESIDENT, and the U.S.A. has that, in spades,” he posted on Truth Social Monday. “There is a SICK conspiracy going on against AI and Data Centers.” It was the first of many aggressively pro-AI pos
title: As White House shields the AI gold rush, Trump family and other allies strike it rich – with few guardrails

author: Chris Stein in Washington
description:
Candidates have been selected for November’s midterms – have Republicans and Democrats made the right choices?

Primary season has official concluded in the United States, with Democrats leading the polls among voters amid widespread economic anxieties, a war with Iran and Donald Trump’s mass deportation agenda continuing into the end of the year.

Democratic and Republican voters have selected contenders for key races in the 3 November midterms that will decide the balance of power in Congress, and the future of both parties. Democrats have been rocked by the primary victories of leftwing candidates. Republicans have doubled down on backing the president’s policies, despite his low approval ratings. And both parties are navigating the fallout from a series of scandals that have forced some candidates from the race, while others decided to press on.
title: Leftists make waves and Trump flexes muscles: US primary season takeaways

author: Petra Stock
description:
The Warsaw event saw 26 teams compete across a series of demanding tasks, inspired - to varying degrees - by tram drivers’ day-to-day tasks

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

It’s the grand final for gunzels. But despite having one of the largest tram networks in the world, Melbourne’s Tramaroos finished second last at this year’s European TramDriver Championship, just ahead of London.

The event, held in Warsaw on Saturday, saw 26 teams compete across a series of demanding tasks, inspired – to varying degrees – by tram drivers’ day-to-day work.

Continue rea
title: The gunzels’ grand final: Melbourne Tramaroos’ campaign derails at European TramDriver Championship

author: Tobi Thomas Health and inequalities correspondent
description:
Exclusive: Analysis ‘lays bare’ something midwives already know from their day-to-day work

About 20,000 disclosures of domestic abuse are estimated to be made to maternity services in England every year, analysis has found.

The figures are likely to be an underestimate of the true scale of disclosures, according to experts, highlighting the role maternity professionals play in identifying abuse.

Continue reading...
title: Thousands of pregnant women in England are reporting domestic abuse. Midwives are struggling to cope

author: Rebecca Bailey China correspondent
description:
Beijing believes slowdown calls aim to lock in US advantage, and is pursuing a different balance between safety and pace

About two years ago, education entrepreneur Boris But had what he calls a “penny-drop moment” – that, like countless others in China, his company needed to embrace AI before it was made obsolete by it.

His clients, well-off parents looking to send their children to study overseas, had begun arriving in his office reeling off information and opinions gleaned not from rival firms, but from chatbots.

Continue reading...
title: Why China is pushing back on US warnings over rapid AI development

author: Gwyn Topham Transport correspondent
description:
Operator that runs services between London Marylebone and Birmingham is sixth to be nationalised since 2025

Chiltern Railways has become the latest train operator to enter public ownership as the government closes in on its ambition to renationalise all major passenger rail services.

The operator, which runs commuter rail services on the Chiltern mainline between London Marylebone and Birmingham, on Sunday became the sixth to be nationalised under Labour, with the remaining four to follow by the end of 2027.

Continue reading...
title: Chiltern Railways enters public ownership in Labour nationalisation push

author: Rowena Mason Whitehall editor
description:
Reform leader also tells US event Europe should have ‘more sensible view’ of president’s administration

Nigel Farage has said he wants to “hijack” Donald Trump’s hardline ICE adviser and bring him to the UK “to secure our borders”.

Speaking at an event in the US, the Reform UK leader also called for Europe to take a “more sensible view” of the US president’s administration rather than seeing it as “villainous”.

Continue reading...
title: Farage says he wants to ‘hijack’ Trump’s ICE czar to help secure UK border

author: Alexandra Topping and Peter Walker
description:
Josh Babarinde wants to target big tech and crypto billionaires while giving power and cash back to the public

Standing outside Toynbee Hall in the East End of London, Josh Babarinde doesn’t exactly look like a rabble-rouser. But despite the well-cut suit and disarmingly large smile, the president of the Liberal Democrats is, apparently, up for a fight.

“There are big modern giants that are getting in the way of people’s ability to thrive, and it is the job of Liberal Democrats to address that,” says the 33-year-old. “How are we going to do that? Well, first of all, we’ve got to flip the table over and rise up.”

Continue reading...
title: ‘Flip the table and rise up’: Lib Dems’ president in combative mood as party gathers in Brighton

author: Penry Buckley
description:
Crime scene established at Waratah Road, Valley Heights as NSW police say they ‘are not looking for any other people at this time’

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A child has died in a stabbing attack in the Blue Mountains, with two other children and a woman in hospital in critical condition, New South Wales police say.

In a statement on Sunday afternoon, police said emergency services responded to reports of three children and a woman with
title: One child dead and two children and woman in critical condition after Blue Mountains stabbing

author: Australian Associated Press and Sarah Basford Canales
description:
Treasury’s latest intergenerational report projects life expectancy at birth will reach 89 for women and 86 for men by 2066

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Australian households will shrink but more people can expect to live well into their 90s, according to the latest update to forecasts of the country’s long-term future.

Treasury’s latest intergenerational report, to be published in full on Monday, will project the impact of government pol
title: More Australians to live into their 90s as life expectancy forecast to rise over coming decades

author: Deborah Cole in Berlin
description:
Embattled Friedrich Merz faces nervous wait while far-right Alternative für Deutschland party targets further gains

Voters in two German states are going to the polls with the political future of the embattled chancellor, Friedrich Merz, hanging in the balance and an emboldened far right targeting further gains.

Coming two weeks after a seismic election in Saxony-Anhalt in which the anti-immigration, pro-Kremlin Alternative für Deutschland (AfD) scored its highest ever result in a regional poll, the nativist party is expected to drain support again from Merz’s conservative Christian Democratic Union (CDU).

Continue reading...
title: Future of German chancellor hangs in the balance as two states go to polls

author: Australian Associated Press and Guardian staff
description:
Three women were killed in separate incidents just hours apart in NSW on Saturday

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Three women have died just hours apart in separate incidents in one state, including an elderly woman who was fatally stabbed in an alleged domestic violence attack.

A 47-year-old man has been charged with murder after the woman in her 90s was found with stab wounds inside her unit at Sydney’s Bondi Beach at about 5.15pm on Satur
title: Man charged with stabbing murder of 90-year-old woman in Bondi Beach amid spate of alleged domestic violence killings

author: Uwa Ede-Osifo
description:
Bills signed by California governor safeguard vote by mail and make seizing ballots or election records a felony

California governor Gavin Newsom has signed off on a package of bills aimed at bolstering election security, including measures to thwart federal political interference, his office announced on Sunday.

The pieces of legislation appear to address hot button national and state electoral issues, including an extension to the hours for mail-in voting drop off locations.

Continue reading...
title: Gavin Newsom signs election security bills to thwart federal interference by Trump
